title: Sound crackles, pops or sounds distorted on speakers or headphones
symptoms: Music, videos or system sounds crackle, pop or sound distorted
Audio sounds harsh or 'fuzzy' even at normal volume
Crackling started after a driver or Windows update
causes: Audio enhancements (driver effects such as loudness, bass boost or vendor audio suites) are distorting the signal
The default audio format (sample rate and bit depth) does not suit the device or driver
The audio driver is outdated or damaged

signals: Audio enhancements are turned on for the default playback device
Default playback device has a non-default or unusual default format (for example 24-bit 192000 Hz)
Audio device driver is old or shows a problem status in Device Manager

fixes.title: Turn off audio enhancements for the output device
steps: Windows 11: open Settings > System > Sound, select your device under Output, and set Audio enhancements to Off.
Windows 10: right-click the volume icon, select Sounds, open the Playback tab, select your device and choose Properties.
On the Enhancements tab, select Disable all enhancements, then select OK.
If there is no Enhancements tab, open the Advanced tab and clear Enable audio enhancements.
Play audio again and check whether the crackling is gone.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft 'Fix distorted or crackling audio in Windows' page; first listed fix
Microsoft Q&A community answer (not accepted) marked helpful by 10+ people; poster reports disabling enhancements, exclusive mode and hardware acceleration stopped the crackling

fixes.title: Try a different default audio format
steps: Windows 11: open Settings > System > Sound, select your device under Output, and select Advanced.
Windows 10: right-click the volume icon, select Sounds, select your device on the Playback tab, choose Properties and open the Advanced tab.
Under Default format, choose a different format, such as 24 bit, 48000 Hz or 16 bit, 48000 Hz.
Select OK and test your audio. Try one format at a time.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page; 'Change the default audio format' fix
Native Instruments official Windows tuning guide; says mismatched sample rates between Windows and audio software cause serious problems

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the audio driver
steps: Open Device Manager from the Start menu.
Expand Sound, video and game controllers, right-click your audio device and select Update driver.
Restart the PC and test the audio.
If the problem continues, install the latest audio driver from your PC, motherboard or audio interface manufacturer's website.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page; 'Update or reinstall the audio driver' fix
Engine DJ (inMusic) official support article; lists installing the newest audio driver as a quick fix for crackles and dropouts

title: Crackling or dropouts caused by power-saving settings
symptoms: Audio crackles or drops out, often on a laptop or on battery
Crackling is worse when the PC is idle or lightly loaded
Crackling started after switching to a Balanced or Power saver plan
causes: The CPU drops into low-power states or low clock speeds and the audio buffer runs empty
USB selective suspend powers down a USB audio device or hub
Laptop vendor power utilities override Windows power settings

signals: Active power plan is Power saver or Balanced
Minimum processor state in the active plan is low (for example 5%)
USB selective suspend is enabled while a USB audio device is in use

fixes.title: Switch to the High performance power plan
steps: Open Control Panel > System and Security > Power Options.
Select High performance. If it is not shown, select Show additional plans first.
Test your audio.
To undo, select your previous plan (usually Balanced) again.

sources.signal: Native Instruments official Windows tuning guide; High Performance plan listed for crackles and dropouts
Engine DJ (inMusic) official support article; recommends High Performance power plan on laptops

fixes.title: Raise minimum processor state and turn off USB selective suspend
steps: Open Control Panel > Power Options and select Change plan settings for the active plan.
Select Change advanced power settings.
Set Processor power management > Minimum processor state to 100%.
Set USB settings > USB selective suspend setting to Disabled.
Select OK and test your audio. This uses more power and can make a laptop run warmer.

sources.signal: Native Instruments official guide; gives these exact advanced power settings (minimum processor state 100%, USB selective suspend Disabled)
Engine DJ (inMusic) official support article; advises disabling aggressive power-saving features for dropouts

title: Clicks, pops or dropouts caused by high DPC latency from another driver
symptoms: Audio clicks, pops or drops out at random, even with enhancements off
Glitches happen when downloading, using Wi-Fi, or when the GPU is busy
LatencyMon says the system is not suitable for real-time audio
causes: A network, Wi-Fi, graphics, storage, USB or ACPI driver holds the CPU too long (high DPC/ISR latency)
Outdated chipset, BIOS or device drivers

signals: Audio glitches correlate with network or GPU activity
A latency monitor reports high DPC execution time for drivers such as ndis.sys, tcpip.sys, nvlddmkm.sys, dxgkrnl.sys, storport.sys or acpi.sys

fixes.title: Install Windows updates and update chipset, network and graphics drivers
steps: Install all available updates in Windows Update and restart.
Install the latest chipset, network (Wi-Fi and Ethernet) and graphics drivers from your PC or motherboard manufacturer's website.
Check Device Manager for devices with a warning icon and update their drivers.
Restart and test your audio.

sources.signal: Native Instruments official guide; driver-by-driver table (ndis.sys, nvlddmkm.sys, storport.sys etc.) recommending updates
Engine DJ (inMusic) official DPC latency article; update Windows, network and flagged drivers

fixes.title: Temporarily disable Wi-Fi or network adapters to test for network-driver latency
steps: Open Device Manager and expand Network adapters.
Right-click the Wi-Fi adapter and select Disable device. Do not uninstall it. You will lose internet access while it is disabled.
Play audio and check whether the clicks and dropouts stop.
If they stop, re-enable the adapter and install the newest network driver from the manufacturer.
Right-click the adapter and select Enable device to undo.

sources.signal: Native Instruments official guide; for ndis.sys/tcpip.sys latency, disable network adapters while using audio and re-enable afterwards
Engine DJ (inMusic) official article; disable Wi-Fi in Device Manager and compare latency with it off and on

title: Distortion or crackles when the Windows sample rate does not match the app or audio interface
symptoms: Audio crackles or sounds wrong only in one music, DAW or recording app
Sound is distorted after changing the sample rate in an audio app or interface
Pitch or speed sounds slightly off
causes: The Windows default format (for example 44100 Hz) differs from the rate used by the app or audio interface (for example 48000 Hz)

signals: The default format sample rate of the playback device differs from the rate set in the audio interface control panel or app

fixes.title: Set the Windows default format to the same sample rate as your app or interface
steps: Find the sample rate your audio app or interface uses (often 44100 Hz or 48000 Hz).
Windows 11: open Settings > System > Sound, select your device, and select Advanced. Windows 10: open Sounds > Playback > device Properties > Advanced.
Under Default format, select the format with the same sample rate.
Select OK, restart the audio app, and test.

sources.signal: Native Instruments official guide; 'Match the sample rate' across Windows and audio software
Official Microsoft page; documents changing Default format to fix distorted or crackling audio
